description: S459 LOW-4 + MED-1: a write into a refined collection is judged by what it changes, against EVERY position that holds the changed object. (1) `@x = @y` then `@y.push(3)` — the array is held by @y (`number(>5)[]`) and @x (`number(>0)[]`); 3 is refused by @y's type and the array is left unchanged (before the fix the owner map named only @x, the push was admitted, and the trailing setter's refusal never undid it: @y = [6, 7, 3]). (2) the same push through @x. (3) a copy-on-write field write `@rows[1].n = -5` and (4) a row write `@rows[0] = { …, n: -5 }` are judged at the path. (5) an array held at two positions of one struct value (`@p.b = @p.a`) refuses a push that one position's type refuses. (6) a push into a nested array `@mm[1].push(-5)`. Every refused write throws E-CONTRACT-001-RT and every cell keeps its prior value.
rationale: §53.3.3: "the compiler-generated check SHALL throw a runtime error with code E-CONTRACT-001-RT before the assignment is applied. The variable retains its prior value." §53.1: the check is "an O(1) boolean expression" over the incoming value — the element or field written, not the whole collection.
